Q1 2025 Pharma Biotools VC Trends
VC activity
Quarter highlights
Funding activity sees a strong rebound: Investment in pharma biotools has mirrored that of 
broader biopharma cycles. After peaking in 2020-2021 at $10.4 billion across 430 deals, funding 
corrected through 2022-2023 before beginning to resurge in 2024. Q1 2025 demonstrated a strong 
rebound, recording 65 deals (up 8.3% from Q4 2024) with $1.3 billion in funding. This marked an 
81.4% quarterly increase and the highest level of investment since Q2 2024. However, the industry 
is very consolidated, with fewer but massive deals driven by intellectual property and patents.
Investors shift toward higher-value deals: In the trailing 12 months, deal activity declined 9.5% 
to 238 deals, but total funding increased 12.8% to $4.8 billion, indicating larger average deal sizes 
and investor focus on more mature opportunities. This trend suggests market stabilization around 
selective, quality-focused investments while maintaining robust capital deployment.
Investment trends and market dynamics
AI and computational biology lead investment focus: AI-driven drug discovery, synthetic biology, 
and next-generation sequencing remain top targets, with computational biology platforms seeing 
particularly strong interest. Investors increasingly favor multiapplication platforms over single-
product plays, driving consolidation around companies with broad technology applicability.
Emerging technology areas gain momentum: Lab automation and computational tools have 
continued to attract sustained interest, while diagnostic multiomics platforms have gained 
significant momentum as personalized medicine adoption accelerates. Spatial biology, single-cell 
analysis tools, and AI-powered laboratory management systems are attracting growing investor 
attention as the industry pushes toward more integrated, data-driven research environments.

Q1 2025 Pharma Biotools VC Trends
VC ACTIVITY
Strategic consolidation continues: Mature platforms continue to draw strategic M&A from 
industry giants such as Thermo Fisher Scientific and Danaher Corporation (exemplified by Thermo 
Fisher’s acquisition of Olink and Danaher’s acquisition of Abcam), while advanced and emerging 
technologies secure the majority of new venture dollars.
Notable Q1 2025 VC deals
Megarounds of $100 million or more dominate funding:
•	 Colossal Biosciences raised a $200 million Series C for its CRISPR-based de-extinction and 
synthetic biology platform, reaching a $10.2 billion post-money valuation.
•	 Harrison.ai closed a $111.8 million Series C for its AI-enabled healthcare-platform 
integration tools.
•	 Geneoscopy completed a $105 million Series C for its digestive disease diagnostics technology, 
achieving a $440 million post-money valuation.
AI-driven platforms attract significant capital:
•	 Chai Discovery secured a $60 million Series A1 for its molecular-structure prediction platform, 
reaching a $570 million post-money valuation.
•	 Bioptimus attracted a $41.4 million Series A to develop its universal AI foundation model 
for biology.
•	 Latent Labs garnered a $39.9 million Series A for continuing work on its AI-driven generative 
models for programmable biology.
•	 Zafrens obtained a $23 million Series A for its cell-drug interaction mapping technology.
Specialized technology segments show strong activity:
•	 Stellaromics completed a $80 million Series B to research spatial biology and gene expression 
analysis technology.
•	 Quibim closed a $50 million Series A to design multiomics analytical tools for precision 
health imaging.
•	 Atrandi Biosciences raised a $25 million Series A for its microfluidics technology platform.
•	 Wheeler Bio secured a $36 million Series A1 for its biomanufacturing services.
•	 Exothera garnered $33.2 million for its research in viral vector manufacturing services.
Exit activity and M&A
Exit activity remains at low levels: Q1 2025 recorded six exits generating $0.2 billion in total value, 
consistent with the subdued exit environment that has persisted since 2022. The quarter included 
one public listing and five acquisitions, a continuation of the correction after 2021, when exits 
peaked at $47.3 billion across 46 transactions.

CONFIDENTIAL. NOT FOR REDISTRIBUTION.  PG 7
Q1 2025 Pharma Biotools VC Trends
Strategic acquisitions dominate the exit landscape: Notable exits included chromatography 
product developer Sepax Technologies’ $217 million IPO (the quarter’s largest exit) and the 
strategic acquisitions of five companies: SeQure DX (acquired for $7 million by MaxCyte), Eagle 
Genomics, Asia Genomics, Coriell Life Sciences, and Molecular Assemblies (acquired by Maravai 
LifeSciences). Most transactions involved undisclosed terms, suggesting smaller deal sizes and 
strategic rather than financial buyer interest.
Consolidations focus on complementary technologies: Strategic buyers continue focusing on 
genomics, diagnostics, and analytical tools that enhance existing product portfolios. The low exit 
volume indicates continued pressure on liquidity events, with strategic M&A providing the primary 
path to exit for biotools companies. Exit activity remains well below the sector’s historical peak 
between 2020 and 2022, when quarterly exit values regularly exceeded $8 billion to $47 billion.
2025 outlook
Capital allocation trends favor proven platforms: Biotools capital allocation is expected to 
continue consolidating into fewer but larger deals, with investors prioritizing platform technologies 
with validated performance data and clear market adoption pathways. This reflects the sector’s 
maturation and increasing focus on companies with proven commercial traction, particularly 
favoring AI-driven platforms and multiapplication tools over single-product solutions.
VC ACTIVITY
Mixed market sentiment emerges amid macroeconomic headwinds: The 2025 J.P. Morgan 
Healthcare Conference initially set an optimistic tone, driven by renewed interest in life sciences 
tool innovation and AI-powered drug discovery advances. However, persistent macroeconomic 
pressures and funding constraints in academic markets continue directing investor focus toward 
established companies with diversified customer bases and recurring revenue models.
Strategic M&A: Opportunities for acquisitions are expected to grow throughout 2025, as large life 
sciences tool companies such as Thermo Fisher Scientific and Danaher Corporation may seek to 
expand their portfolios with innovative technologies. The prevailing funding environment could 
present attractive acquisition prospects at more reasonable valuations. Additionally, strategic 
buyers could utilize ample cash reserves to bolster technological capabilities during this period.
Early-stage funding remains constrained: Seed and early-stage biotools investments face 
significant headwinds as venture funds maintain capital discipline, primarily directing allocation 
to follow-on investments in proven platform companies rather than new opportunities. The 
challenging funding environment at academic institutions, combined with weak exit activity 
and limited IPO opportunities, will likely constrain capital recycling in the early-stage segment 
throughout 2025.
